chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Anbasa ibn Bajad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
‘Never was a meal presented to Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him) in which were dates, except that he (peace be upon him) began with the dates’.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for starting a meal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the Sunnah of prioritizing dates at the start of a meal, a practice rooted in the Prophet's daily routine and spiritual gratitude. It reflects the Islamic emphasis on simplicity and the blessing (barakah) associated with this specific fruit, often cited alongside the concept of 'breaking fast' or starting meals with wholesome, natural foods.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Anbasa Bin Bajad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Never was a meal presented to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> in which were dates, except that he<sup>saww</sup> began with the dates’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from ibn Sinan from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from ‘ Anbasah ibn Bijad who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Whenever food was brought to the Messenger of Allah in which there were dates, he began with dates.’”
